instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1-inch chunks. Put them in a pot, cover with cold water, bring to a boil, then simmer for about 12 minutes, until a fork slides in easily. Drain and leave them in the pot to steam dry.
Meanwhile, rinse the spinach and drain it well. Seed and finely chop the chili, mince the ginger, and roughly chop the cilantro, leaves and tender stems. That should be about 1/2 cup.
Heat a dry skillet over medium-low. Add the chickpea flour and stir for about 2 minutes, until it smells nutty. Transfer it to a plate.
Pulse the poha in a blender for about 20 seconds, until it's a fine powder. Add it to the plate with the chickpea flour.
Heat 1 tsp of the oil in the large skillet over medium. Add the ginger and chili and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the peas and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're soft.
Add the spinach and stir for about 2 minutes, until it wilts. Spread everything on a plate and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Mash the potatoes in a large bowl until smooth with no lumps.
Blend the cooled peas and spinach with the cilantro until you have a smooth green paste, without adding water. Scrape down the sides as you go.

Add the paste, the chickpea flour and poha, the salt, garam masala and chaat masala to the potatoes. Mix to a firm dough that doesn't stick to your hands. If it feels sticky, let it sit for 5 minutes and mix again.
Taste a little of the mixture. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Divide the dough into 10 portions and flatten each into a patty about 1/2 inch thick.
Heat 3/4 tbsp of the remaining oil in the large skillet over medium. Add 5 patties and cook for about 3 minutes per side, until golden and crisp. Flip each one once and gently. Transfer to a plate.
Add the last 3/4 tbsp oil and cook the other 5 patties the same way.
method_notes: Indian Healthy Recipes (the lead) boils the potatoes, wilts spinach with peas, grinds that into a paste, and folds it into the mashed potato with roasted gram flour, breadcrumbs and a few spices before pan frying. Hebbar's Kitchen adds beans, capsicum and paneer, uses a cashew in each tikki and deep fries. This version follows the lead's pan fry and swaps the breadcrumbs for powdered poha so it stays gluten-free.
